prompts.text: If our friend group had an award for arriving exactly when food is ready, who would win?
The friend who remembers everybody's birthday deserves a trophy, not more group-chat responsibilities.
We have to give each other completely ridiculous awards at dinner. What's mine?
Winning 'best emergency advice' or 'most dramatic retelling of a normal event'?
Tell me about a time someone's usual role in the group was completely reversed.
Every group has a friend whose 'I'm five minutes away' is an entire genre of fiction.
Which of us would win an award for making friends with the person serving the food?
A stranger asks which one of us is the sensible one. Who volunteers before anybody can object?
Being voted the group's official photographer or its designated keeper of lost items?
There should be a category for friends who remember embarrassing details far too accurately.
We all get stuck inside a shopping centre overnight. Who's in charge, and who disappears into the snack aisle?
Which friend would survive longest on a deserted island purely by talking their way out of problems?
Our group running a tiny restaurant for a day or attempting to manage a farm for a week?
Most friendship groups would fall apart at the stage of agreeing on what to name their imaginary boat.
Tell me about a time your group made a tiny problem sound like a national emergency.
The most confident person explaining directions is not always the one who knows the way.
We're contestants on a game show where nobody understands the rules. Who somehow wins?
If our group had to build a tent without instructions, who would claim they knew exactly what to do?
Getting lost together in an enormous museum or trying to escape a maze made of hedges?
The friend who stays calm when everyone panics is secretly the funniest person to watch.
What's the food opinion you could defend against the entire group for no good reason?
One plate of jollof rice arrives and everyone says they're not hungry. Who takes the first spoon?
Plantain that's very ripe and sweet or plantain with a little bite left in it?
Somebody always insists they're just tasting your chips and then eats half of them.
The person who says 'anything is fine' should not be allowed to reject six restaurant suggestions.
Tell me about a group meal where the debate over what to order lasted longer than the meal.
Which friend's food recommendation sounds questionable but usually turns out excellent?
We open a one-day food stall and can only sell one thing. Who should be trusted with the menu?
A competitive blind taste test or making a meal where everyone contributes a mystery ingredient?
A shared plate of snacks will reveal every friendship group's unspoken rules about fairness.
Which message in our group chat deserves to be printed, framed and hung in a gallery?
Every group chat has one sticker that means absolutely nothing to anybody outside it.
Someone accidentally sends a dramatic voice note meant for their boss. Do we delete it or hold an emergency meeting?
A week where everyone must communicate in GIFs or a day where nobody can send voice notes?
The 'typing...' bubble has caused more unnecessary suspense than some entire television series.
Tell me about an inside joke that makes no sense when you try to explain its origin.
Which friend would accidentally turn a quiet group chat into an argument about breakfast?
Our chat history is turned into a documentary. What's the scene the editors simply cannot explain?
An archive of the funniest screenshots or a playlist of our most chaotic voice notes?
The person who hardly ever writes often returns with the comment that ends the discussion.
Who in the group gets control of the music and immediately abuses the privilege?
We're one hour into a road trip when someone realises their bag is still at home. What's our group policy?
Stopping at every interesting roadside stall or driving straight through to get there early?
A road trip is a personality test disguised as transport.
Tell me about the funniest disagreement you've seen over who gets the front seat.
The friend who insists they don't get hungry on journeys is usually first to ask about snacks.
Which of our friends would start a singalong while everyone else was trying to sleep?
The navigation system says turn left but your confident friend says right. Whose instruction wins?
A carefully planned playlist or giving each passenger one surprise song every hour?
The person who packs thirty 'essentials' should be responsible for carrying all thirty.
